newsitem.title: CHINA: China refinery plans 689 mln yuan A share IPO.
newsitem.headline: China refinery plans 689 mln yuan A share IPO.

text.p: Chinese oil refiner Shijiazhuang Petrochemical Co Ltd said on Tuesday it planned to raise net proceeds of 688.8 million yuan from an initial public offering (IPO) of 120 million A shares.
The company would launch the IPO, priced at 5.89 yuan each, on the Shenzhen bourse between July 11 and July 18, it said in an issue prospectus in the Shenzhen-based Securities Times.
The company, based in the northern province of Hebei, had an annual crude oil refining capacity of 3.5 million tonnes, the prospectus said.
Most of the crude oil, which accounted for 78 percent of the firm's production costs, was supplied by China National Petrochemical Corporation, it said.
Shijiazhuang Petrochemical said it would channel all proceeds into a 3.57 billion yuan petrochemical joint-venture, the construction of which began in 1996 for completion in 1999, it said.
The project was financed by a 1.9 billion yuan loan from an Italian bank at 6.95 percent interest per annum, it said.
Shijiazhuang Petrochemical forecast net profits of 209 million yuan for 1997, compared with 245 million in 1996 and 297 million in 1995 under Chinese accounting standards.
It did not explain the projected earnings slide.
Sales for 1997 were targeted at 3.38 billion yuan, against 2.92 billion last year and 2.95 billion in 1995, according to the prospectus.
Diesel accounted for 41.7 percent of its sales in 1996, with gasoline accounting for 40.5 percent, it showed.
The firm had a total of 600 million state institutional shares, it said, adding that China Guotai Securities Co was the chief underwriter for the IPO.
